Something I’ve been building quietly for six years — and obsessively for the last eight months.
 
I wanted Seven Seven Six 7️⃣7️⃣6️⃣ to be the first software company that deploys venture capital. With Cerebro, it feels like we’re finally getting close.
 
Cerebro started as the operating system that runs everything at 776. You can see our live user metrics on sevensevensix.com
 
I spent five years sweating every pixel of the UI/UX. The punchline? I now touch that interface maybe an hour a day. Everything else runs on top of the Cerebro MCP.
 
Most firms operate on relationships stored in someone’s head and a CRM nobody updates. We built the opposite: a system that has captured six years of the firm’s memory — every meeting, every pitch we ever took, every note, every founder interaction — and makes all of it queryable.
 
That’s the part I’d point any partner to. A CRM stores contacts. Cerebro stores judgment — six years of how we evaluated companies, what we saw early, who we backed and why. It’s a proprietary dataset no one can buy, and it gets more valuable every single day we operate.
 
The unlock is the Cerebro MCP. I ask in plain language — “give me the full history on this company” — and it assembles six years of context in seconds. Our head of engineering Asif Ahmed and I build most of it through Claude Code. (Disclosure: 776 is on Anthropic’s cap table.)
 
In practice, it’s an AI chief of staff. Every morning it preps me for every meeting with the entire relevant history — every prior conversation, every note anyone at the firm ever logged — before I walk in the room. Better prep means we show up sharper for our founders.
 
It also makes us better partners after the check. It reads the full context of a relationship and flags where a founder might need us before they ask — an intro, a follow-up, a problem forming early. The whole point is to serve the portfolio faster than any human system could.
 
And it holds me accountable. After meetings it tells me what I could’ve done better — a pitch, a portfolio sales call, a team sync. A firm that critiques itself compounds. One that doesn’t, drifts.
 
We ship constantly. The app is on TestFlight for our team and founders — no public release to manage, no waiting on App Store review. New capability in our hands the same week we build it. That velocity is the moat, not any single feature.
 
So tldr.cerebro.ai is a living log — because the software changes faster than any demo could keep up with. We’ll post what we build as we build it, in the open.
 
The bet underneath all of it: the enduring edge in venture isn’t the biggest team or the loudest brand. It’s proprietary memory that compounds.
 
We’ve been quietly building that asset for six years. We’re still on the starting line.

Thank you, Sports Illustrated! I feel so blessed that my second chapter (life after Reddit) would get so big, so fast, and most importantly — be so damn fulfilling. I'm very proud my daughters get to see me building this legacy in women's sports and beyond, especially in the AI revolution, sports will only get more valuable because we can't replace the humanity on the pitch, track, court, etc.

My mom's fight with teminal brain cancer in the early days of founding @Reddit taught me the importance of caregivers. I saw my dad step up into this role while also running his own small business.

Most Americans aren't so lucky: the emotional toll, out-of-pocket expenses, and the abysmal lack of paid family and medical leave in the US means too many family members are forced to choose between caregiving and a full-time job.

This is why @776fund led the seed round in @join_aidaly whose mission is to provide access to compensation and financial services for family caregivers. Aidaly ensures that the caregiving experience is not more difficult than it needs to be and that caregivers are able to focus on what matters most—their loved one.
